projects.name: Green Volt
projects.sourceStatus: Active development / pre-FID; consented, option agreement secured, CfD awarded

factClaims.value: Active development / pre-FID; consented, option agreement secured, CfD awarded
factClaims.note: Current assessment combines development status, consent, lease-option, CfD, FEED, and 2026 survey evidence.
FID / financial close has not been verified in public primary sources as of 2026-09-02.
Project source states up to 35 floating wind turbines.
Sources distinguish targeted first power in 2029 from estimated COD in 2030; current public evidence is insufficient to treat either as a committed COD.

intelligence.currentAssessment: Active / Pre-FID. Green Volt has full onshore and offshore consent, a Crown Estate Scotland option agreement, and a 400 MW AR6 CfD, while 2025-2026 FEED, land-access, and survey activity show continuing development. Construction is not yet committed because no public FID or financial close announcement was verified and oil-and-gas offtake remains a material open gate after Buzzard electrification was reportedly dropped.
intelligence.fidStatus: No public FID or financial close announcement verified as of 2026-09-02; latest public evidence still frames FID as a future 2026 decision rather than an achieved milestone.

confirmedFacts.text: Scottish Ministers granted offshore consent and marine licences on 19 April 2024; Aberdeenshire Council granted onshore infrastructure consent on 21 March 2024.
Crown Estate Scotland entered into an Option Agreement with Flotation Energy and Vårgrønn for Green Volt on 19 April 2024.
DESNZ AR6 results awarded Green Volt Offshore Windfarm (GV01) 400 MW of Floating Offshore Wind CfD support for delivery year 2028/29 at 139.93 GBP/MWh in 2012 prices.
Green Volt awarded Worley the onshore substation FEED contract in July 2025.
Ofgem granted consent in January 2026 for Green Volt to exercise statutory rights of entry for survey work on remaining land along the planned cable corridor.
Green Volt reported continuing 2026 onshore and nearshore survey work to inform civil, cable, system, and construction methodology design.

editorialInferences.text: Consent + option agreement + CfD + FEED and survey activity imply an active pre-construction project, not a cancelled or paused project.
400 MW CfD support + 560 MW project capacity + reported loss of the Buzzard electrification route imply revenue support is meaningful but does not resolve the INTOG oil-and-gas offtake gate.
The absence of a verified FID announcement, together with SDI's January 2026 description of FID as estimated in 2026, supports treating Green Volt as pre-FID.

currentGates: Current electricity offtake agreement for oil-and-gas installation supply
Firm turbine and floating-platform supply decisions
Progression from Crown Estate Scotland option agreement to lease
watchpoints: Named replacement or confirmed oil-and-gas offtake agreement
Crown Estate Scotland lease step-through for Green Volt
Turbine, floater, cable, mooring, or EPCI contract awards
Start of fabrication, onshore substation construction, or offshore installation
unresolvedUncertainties: FID / financial close date is UNKNOWN.
Committed COD is UNKNOWN; public sources cite first power and estimated COD targets but not a committed COD.
Oil-and-gas offtake counterparties are UNKNOWN after the reported Buzzard setback.
Turbine OEM, floater technology, mooring, cable, and EPCI suppliers are UNKNOWN.
Whether the full 560 MW project can proceed under the current commercial structure remains an inference, not a confirmed fact.
